question: explain data engineering in simple words
draft: Data engineering involves developing, implementing, and maintaining systems and processes that handle raw data, transforming it into high-quality, consistent information for use by data scientists, analysts, and other stakeholders [Ch. 1]. It encompasses the movement, manipulation, and management of data [Ch. 1], and is the intersection of security, data management, DataOps, data architecture, orchestration, and software engineering [Ch. 1]. The core purpose is to design robust and reliable systems to carry data through its lifecycle and serve it according to end-user needs [Ch. 4]. Data engineers ensure data remains available and usable, setting up and operating the organization’s data infrastructure [Ch. 1].

[Ch. 1] It's easy to focus on new tech and forget the main goal of data engineering. [Ch. 4] Data engineers keep data available for others to use. [Ch. 1]
quotes: When we unpack the common threads of how various people define data engineering, an obvious pattern emerges: a data engineer gets data, stores it, and prepares it for consumption by data scientists, analysts, and others.
Data engineering is all about the movement, manipulation, and management of data.

However, it’s easy to get caught up in chasing bleeding-edge technology while losing sight of the core purpose of data engineering: designing robust and reliable systems to carry data through the full lifecycle and serve it according to the needs of end users.
It takes dedicated specialists—data engineers—to maintain data so that it remains available and usable by others.

question: explain what a watermark is in simple words
draft: A watermark is a threshold used by a window to determine whether data in a window is within the established time interval or whether it is considered late-arriving data. [Ch. 8]

before.answer: A watermark checks if data is on time or late. [Ch. 8]

question: explain CRUD in simple words
draft: CRUD stands for create, read, update, and delete, which are the four basic operations of persistent storage [Ch. 5]. It is a common pattern used in programming and databases, representing how data is managed [Ch. 5]. When using CRUD, data must first be created before it can be read, updated, or deleted [Ch. 5]. CRUD is widely used in software applications, such as web applications that use RESTful HTTP requests and databases [Ch. 5].

question: explain batch and streaming in simple words
draft: Batch processing involves handling data in large chunks, typically on a predetermined schedule or when a certain amount of data is accumulated [Ch. 2]. Streaming, on the other hand, processes data in real-time or near real-time, continuously feeding data to downstream systems as it is produced [Ch. 2]. While batch processing is still widely used, especially in analytics and machine learning, streaming is becoming more accessible due to the separation of storage and compute in modern systems [Ch. 2]. Micro-batching is a hybrid approach where batch-oriented frameworks are used to process data in smaller, more frequent batches, typically every two minutes to every second [Ch. 8]. True streaming systems, like Beam and Flink, process data one event at a time, though they may still operate in batches for certain processes [Ch. 8].

before.answer: Batch ingestion processes data in large groups at once. [Ch. 2] Many systems separate storage and computing, making data stream processing easier and more popular. [Ch. 2] A micro-batch runs every two minutes or less. [Ch. 8]
quotes: Batch ingestion is simply a specialized and convenient way of processing this stream in large chunks—for example, handling a full day’s worth of data in a single batch.

However, the separation of storage and compute in many systems and the ubiquity of event-streaming and processing platforms make the continuous processing of data streams much more accessible and increasingly popular.
A micro-batch might run anywhere from every two minutes to every second.

question: explain data ingestion in simple words
draft: Data ingestion is the process of moving data from one place to another, typically from source systems into storage [Ch. 7]. It involves ensuring that data flows consistently and securely to its destination, which can be part of a data pipeline [Ch. 7]. This process can be done in batch, where data is ingested in bulk based on time intervals or the size of accumulated data [Ch. 7]. The exact method can vary depending on the needs of the data engineering lifecycle [Ch. 7].

before.answer: Data ingestion moves data from one place to another. [Ch. 7] Ingestion moves data from one pipe to another. [Ch. 7] Data is taken from a source, based on time or data size. [Ch. 7]
quotes: Data ingestion is the process of moving data from one place to another.
At the heart, ingestion is plumbing, connecting pipes to other pipes, ensuring that data flows consistently and securely to its destination.
This means that data is ingested by taking a subset of data from a source system, based either on a time interval or the size of accumulated data (Figure 7-10).
